bullets.title: MRVL: Investor Day crushes; FY31 $70-90B revenue target, $30+ EPS; PT upgrades across the Street
bullets.body: Marvell hosted its Investor Day raising FY28 revenue guidance to $20B (from ~$18B), FY29 custom silicon to $12B+, and introducing a new FY31 framework of $70-90B revenue and >$30 EPS (~55-60% CAGR). Custom silicon TAM expands to ~$30B by FY31 driven by all four major hyperscalers; interconnect (DSP, scale-up optics, switching) guides to $37.5B. PT upgrades included Piper to $400 (OW), Wolfe to $375 (OP), UBS to $350 (Buy), JPM to $360 (OW), Opco to $425, Roth to $350; TD Cowen upgraded to Buy from Hold with $350 PT. CY30 TAM framed at $400B.

bullets.title: LITE: CEO confirms optical components sold out through early 2029; 70% demand unmet in 2027
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO stated AI server optical components are completely sold out through early 2029—an extension from the prior 2028 timeline—and that the company cannot meet roughly 70% of demand for some products through next year. Stock hit 52-week highs (+567% YTD). Broad read-through to AAOI, COHR, TSEM, CIEN, GLW, FN in sympathy. OCP Summit (Oct 12-15) expected to confirm life-extension of 800G/1.6T pluggables and NPO gaining favor over CPO near-term.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro orders cut 15-20% in October; demand weakest surprise of cycle
bullets.body: Apple instructed suppliers to cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders by at least 15% for October due to soft demand after the $100+ price increase and rising memory costs. Wolfe, Citi, Jefferies, and JPM all highlighted the early timing (Oct 9 vs. typical late-4Q) as a negative signal. PC shipments also fell 20.1% YoY in 3Q26 to 62.7M units, with HP down 30.9% and Dell down 25%; Apple gained 90bps of share. SWKS (~60% AAPL revenue exposure) and QRVO flagged as at-risk. Sep-Q results due Nov 2 with focus on Services growth (~2% YoY App Store).

bullets.title: T/VZ: SpaceX acquires 800MHz low-band spectrum for ~$8B; structural mobile carrier threat crystallizes
bullets.body: SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide 14 MHz 800 MHz spectrum portfolio from Grain Management for ~$8B, completing the missing indoor-penetration piece for Starlink Mobile. T fell ~9-10%, VZ ~10%, TMUS ~12% on the week while tower REITs (AMT, CCI, SBAC) rallied 7-12% on deployment upside. Multiple analyst views: MS models <1% US mobile penetration by 2030 scaling to ~7% by 2035, primarily rural. Citi sizes 21% upside for CCI, 20% SBAC, 10% AMT. At T the JV with GIP/CPP for Forged Fiber 37/Gigapower was announced separately—bullish for deleveraging.

bullets.title: CEG: Announces 890 MW 20-year nuclear deal + 2.7 GW PPA with Google; IPPs re-rated
bullets.body: Constellation Energy confirmed a 20-year, 890 MW new nuclear capacity agreement with Google on the PJM grid (first uprate by 2028) plus a 15-year 2.7 GW existing fleet supply agreement, representing $4.3B+ in new investment. CEG surged ~12% on the week; TLN +18%, VST +15%. Morgan Stanley raised CEG PT to $369 on ~$2.50/share EPS upside. Broader sentiment on IPPs shifted from depressed positioning (3rd percentile) toward re-rating as mega-cap power deals continue without 1-for-1 new generation requirements.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO meeting reinforces power/market-share thesis; $150B buyback drives first broad sponsorship of year
bullets.body: Multiple bank notes cite NVDA CEO meetings emphasizing tokens-per-GW advantage (~3x peers), strong AI share wins, and ASIC displacement confidence. SpaceX's $40B debt financing to buy Nvidia chips (confirmed by multiple sources) validates compute demand narrative. Hedgeye/Piper flag first broad investor sponsorship of the year with investors rotating into NVDA from other semi names. GS noted French CDS and NVDA CDS trade at essentially the same levels—an AI bubble warning. Stock approaching $6T market cap.

bullets.title: AMZN: In discussions to acquire AI startup Decart for ~$7B; outbid NVDA
bullets.body: Amazon is in discussions to acquire Decart (a generative AI startup) for approximately $7B. Decart had previously been in acquisition talks with Nvidia but received higher offers. Anthropic had also pursued Decart and ended its interest as of September 7, 2026. SpaceX and Nebius were also rumored as interested. Decart raised $300M at ~$4B valuation three months prior to August 2026.

bullets.title: TSM: September revenue +55% YoY confirms AI demand intact; FY27-28 capex raised to $85B/$98B
bullets.body: TSMC's September revenue rose ~55% YoY to record NT$1.49tn ($46.7B), beating guidance; N3 capacity still tight. Goldman raises 2027E capex to $85B (from $78B) and 2028E to $98B. TSMC is separately in discussions with Tesla/SpaceX for a potential second US fab cluster in Texas that could exceed the $265B Arizona commitment. TSMC is reporting earnings Thursday Oct 15; focus on 2027+ capex outlook, GM stability (N2 ramp dilution limited), and GenAI supply visibility.

bullets.title: HUBS: 7% RIF (~660 roles) with $65-75M charges; reaffirms FY26 guidance, raises FY30 OM to 30%
bullets.body: HubSpot announced a restructuring eliminating ~7% of the workforce with $65-75M in severance charges, mostly in Q4 FY26. The company simultaneously reaffirmed Q3 and FY26 guidance and raised its FY30 non-GAAP operating margin target to 30% from 25%. Wolfe notes shares trading at ~15x CY28 FCF ex-SBC approaching local minimum; JPM downgraded to Neutral (PT $240 from $268). Market largely ignored the RIF, focusing on revenue re-acceleration outlook.

bullets.title: NFLX: 5% RIF (~850 workers) planned; MS reiterates OW at $80 PT on ad-tier and India growth
bullets.body: Netflix is preparing to lay off approximately 5% of its workforce (~850 employees) according to Puck News, with an announcement as early as the week of Oct 13. Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight at $80 PT (cut from $83 on FX), noting Netflix trades at ~15x FY28 EPS with double-digit revenue growth and 150-200bps margin expansion potential. Ad revenue projected to triple to $4.8B by 2027. Wolfe notes Netflix top 10 viewing fell 11% YoY but shows stabilization vs. Q2's -13%.

bullets.title: SPHR: Down ~40% from mid-August on 2H estimate cuts; 4Q catalyst path rich—new film + venue announcements
bullets.body: Sphere Entertainment has fallen ~40% from mid-August highs as sell-side analysts cut 3Q Wizard of Oz revenue estimates below consensus. Wolfe Research flags this was well-telegraphed 1-2 months prior. Key upcoming catalysts: (1) new large film announcement expected by early 2027, (2) Japan or Orlando venue announcement possible in coming months/quarters. National Harbor, Maryland DC venue already announced for 2030 opening. SPHR was -17% on the week ending Oct 9 but +11.9% YTD.

bullets.title: META: Muse at #1 US App Store for 22 consecutive days; $27-50B revenue opportunity at scale
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent has been the #1 most downloaded US app for over three weeks with 6.6M+ downloads and 1.8M DAUs. Citi upgrades META to Buy with $800 PT, modeling $8B Year-1 Muse revenue (5% take rate on $170B transactions) scaling to $23B+ in a blue-sky scenario. Wolfe sees $30-50B long-term opportunity. META also launched the Personal Agent Protocol open standard (with Sierra) to enable agent-to-business interactions, and banned ByteDance advertising across its apps. Muse reportedly launched ahead of plan due to competitive threat from 'Instinct'.

bullets.title: BKNG/EXPE/ABNB: OTA stocks down 15-25% on agentic AI threat to commission pools
bullets.body: Hedgeye, Morgan Stanley, and Wolfe all hosted calls on Meta Muse and Google's hotel booking AI Mode threatening OTA intermediation. OTA stocks fell 15-25% following agent launches that can now complete bookings without OTA integration, bypassing commission pools. Expedia leads AI readiness scorecard; Booking moved up; Hyatt and Airbnb sit at the bottom. Notably, ABNB CEO Chesky stated the platform will 'probably not' allow third-party agents to directly book stays. Impact seen as negative for OTAs, positive for hotels and consumers.

bullets.title: NOW: Elite-tier partner call shows strong AI SKU adoption with 10-25% spend uplift on renewals
bullets.body: A JPMorgan webinar with CoreX CEO found that all renewing ServiceNow customers are migrating to new AI SKUs with 10-25% average spend uplift (mostly to Advanced tier). Q3 landed on plan; Q4 tracking 35-40% of annual bookings. Strong growth in $1M+ deals and no seat reductions yet from autonomous workers. AI Control Tower well-positioned for governance. Partner expects 2027 growth to exceed 2026, driven by new SKUs and consumption revenue. Wolfe also likes NOW into earnings.

bullets.title: GOOGL: TPU/Anthropic thesis builds to $50-100B EBIT upside by 2028; Waymo as agentic differentiator
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags GOOGL's Anthropic TPU business could contribute $50-100B in 2028 EBIT (each GW sold generates $5-10B) against a $270B Street estimate, implying Street EPS of $18 vs. bull case mid-$20s to $30. Morgan Stanley's MS MSI turned positive, exiting risk-off since July. Waymo is being highlighted as an underappreciated agentic differentiator—JPM models ~1.1B annual trips and $21B revenue by 2032. Gemini Agent for Work launched with multi-model orchestration including Claude.

bullets.title: ANET: Citi initiates Buy $248 PT; Etherlink SU-144 opens $10B scale-up networking TAM with MSFT/META
bullets.body: Citi initiated Arista with a Buy rating and $248 PT (17.6% upside), highlighting the Etherlink SU-144 as the first pure Ethernet scale-up solution competing against NVIDIA's NVLink and UALink. The ESUN standard is imminent; Dell'Oro sizes the TAM at $10B in 2027. Microsoft is collaborating on Maia accelerators and Meta on scale-out. ANET is Citi's #1 networking pick into 2027, with hyperscalers raising 2027 capex growth to >40% YoY.

bullets.title: SPOT: Joe Rogan renewed for ~$250M multi-year; audiobooks expanding to 180+ markets; Buy $620 PT
bullets.body: Spotify confirmed a new multi-year licensing agreement with Joe Rogan estimated at $250M on similar prior terms. Separately, Spotify is expanding audiobooks to 180+ markets, enabling access for 750M+ users—Citi views this as a gross margin tailwind in 2027 via ~10% price increases in new markets. Citi maintains Buy at $620 PT (27x 2027E FCF). Piper Sandler initiated at Neutral $540 citing ad CPM headwinds. Wolfe sees 33.6% gross margin vs. 33.9% consensus.

bullets.title: PLTR: Goldman upgrades to Buy $230 PT; sovereign AI TAM step-change via FDE/verticalization
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral with a $230 price target, citing a step-function change in TAM via sovereign AI deployment and verticalization strategy. The FDE (Forward Deployed Engineer) model with AI automation creates a self-reinforcing competitive moat. PLTR's valuation discount to high-growth software peers (1.2x EV/FCF vs. 3x) is seen as unjustified. PLTR rose ~10% on the week to a 52-week high. TD Cowen also became constructive.

bullets.title: ACN: F4Q26 revenue +7% crushes guidance; FY27 outlook above expectations; Buy reiterated
bullets.body: Accenture's F4Q26 constant-currency revenue growth of +7% significantly exceeded the +1% to +5% guidance range. New bookings re-accelerated to +5% CC YoY from -3% in F3Q. FY27 CC guidance of +3% to +6% is modestly above expectations. ~400+ new clients started advanced AI work in FY26; emerging AI/data partner bookings more than tripled YoY. UBS reiterates Buy at $275 PT; Mizuho raises PT to $241. Analyst Day on Oct 14 expected to clarify 2027+ growth framework. Trump PERM suspension of ACN from H-1B program added shares (+5%) on near-term labor cost tailwinds.

bullets.title: HUT: UBS Buy $143 PT; River Bend Phase 1 on time with 1GW aspiration; WULF expands Muskie to 1GW
bullets.body: UBS site tour of HUT's River Bend (Louisiana) confirms ~1,100 workers on site, structural steel largely complete, Data Hall 1 power expected within months, with Phase 2 land clearing begun—management cites zero gating factors to multi-GW scale. WULF separately amended its AEP Kentucky Power agreement to expand Muskie contracted capacity to 1 GW and accelerated Phase 2 delivery to 2029 from 2030, receiving $100M in winter bill credits. Roth reinstated HUT at Buy $108. Both CORZ and HUT flagged as top picks in AI colocation by UBS.
